I am 48, been at this 30 years. My man and I work the 10.1 mu together — our two children are grown and working in town, so it's just us at home now. The land is split: about 7.5 mu goes to the wheat-maize rotation like most everyone here, and I keep 2.6 mu in cotton because the price was decent last year and I already have the sprayer.

For the wheat this winter past and coming again — I buy improved seed from the shop in town, the same kind my sister-in-law uses, about 25 jin per mu. I put down two bags of compound fertilizer (about 50 jin, the 15-15-15) before I plough, then top-dress with urea when it greens up in spring, maybe 30 jin per mu. I water at jointing, at heading, and at grain-fill — three times from the well. Wheat usually gives me around 450 kg per mu if the spring rains come, less if they don't. I spray once for aphids, sometimes twice if the neighbor's field gets bad.

For summer maize after wheat — I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the dealer pushes that year, everyone buys the same. I put one bag of compound at sowing and then top-dress urea at the big-bell stage, about 25 jin. Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat, once at tasseling is enough if the rains come. I spray for borer once. Gets me 550 kg or so.

Cotton is more work and more worry. I plant improved seed, cover with film. Cotton eats fertilizer — I put compound before planting and urea twice during the season. I have to spray many times — bollworm, aphids, mites — maybe 6 or 7 times through summer. I water twice. If the weather holds I get around 230 kg of seed cotton per mu. If not, less. That's why I don't plant more of it.

I don't like to cut fertilizer. One bad harvest and the whole year is wasted — a few extra bags of urea is just money, but an empty field is a disaster. I do what worked last year and adjust a little.
